calls.response_tail:
The failure is caused by an inverted equality check in [`clinicbench/store.py`](file:///work/clinicbench/store.py#L139-L141):

```python
def _slot_free_for(self, sid, pid):
    x = self.store.slots[sid]
    return x["status"] == "open" or (x["status"] == "held" and x["held_by"] != pid)
```

When a slot is placed on hold for a patient via [`ToolAPI._hold`](file:///work/clinicbench/store.py#L187-L193) (`status="held"`, `held_by=patient_id`), [`ToolAPI._book`](file:///work/clinicbench/store.py#L143-L157) (and [`ToolAPI._move`](file:///work/clinicbench/store.py#L173-L185)) calls `_slot_free_for(slot_id, patient_id)`. Because `_slot_free_for` checks `x["held_by"] != pid` instead of `x["held_by"] == pid`, it returns `False` for the patient holding the slot and returns `slot_taken` (`"That slot is taken."`).

Because `clinicbench/store.py` is frozen instrument code listed in [`docs/phase3-freeze.json`](file:///work/docs/phase3-freeze.json#L9) (not part of the driver), this is a `fix`.

Fixed `ToolAPI._slot_free_for` in [store.py](file:///work/clinicbench/store.py#L139-L141) by changing `x["held_by"] != pid` to `x["held_by"] == pid`, so a held slot is treated as free for the patient who holds it and rejected as `slot_taken` for other patients.

Verified via a `python3` check exercising `ToolAPI.hold`, `ToolAPI._slot_free_for`, and `ToolAPI.book` (`pytest` is not installed in this environment).
